extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), social media managers, and personnel responsible for Army official publications and websites
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for establishing, managing, and publishing official U.S. Army social media accounts, websites, and publications, including roles/responsibilities, content standards, security, registration, archiving, and contracting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanders' authorization and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authorization to establish official social media accounts in compliance with local network restrictions; authorize social media managers to release information on the command’s behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must ensure social media managers are properly trained/certified, have proper equipment and network access, and generally oversee compliance with the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO responsibilities within command
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs for ACOMs, ASCCs, DRUs, or designated representatives will ensure approved social media sites operate within regulation guidelines and provide accurate information; register platforms in the Army social media directory; maintain a roster and network of social media managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs are the local compliance and coordination focal point for social media operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media manager duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage accounts using only authorized Government equipment; ensure sites operate within guidelines and policy; update content regularly and consistently; publish properly reviewed, released, and public domain information; actively engage the public while maintaining security and privacy; archive and close inactive or noncompliant accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must not release unreleased or FOUO content, must develop/update local SOPs, treat social media access/passwords with care equivalent to PII, and maintain continuity documentation including rosters, processes, and appointment letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and documentation for social media sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a continuity book or file for approved social media sites used in support of the brigade or installation mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity should include roster of authorized accounts and administrators; social media processes and strategy (including public defacement response plan and justification for platform use); and appointment letters for each unit’s social media manager(s). Appointment letters and sites must be reviewed annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel who manage and release information on official Army social media platforms must be OPSEC level II certified and be current with required social media training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required for release authority; social media managers registered in the directory must meet occupational specialty and training prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration in Army social media directory
rubrics_metrics.description: The social media directory registers official social media accounts of organizations with appropriate civilian or military occupational specialties and release authority; pages must be open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private groups, accounts, or feeds will not be registered; registration requirements include OPSEC level II training and release authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release authority for social media managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media managers must be granted release authority by the commanding officer to manage and release information on official accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release authority must be renewed during command and personnel changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account labeling and user terms of agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Army social media platforms must be labeled as an official account and classified as a Government organization; user terms must include general, privacy/security, copyright/trademark, moderated account disclaimers, FOIA notice, and specific wording per GSA negotiated terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information must be a valid .mil or .gov email address and the account must use an official URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication priorities and forbidden topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations will maintain a list of communication priorities as a basis for posts and a working list of topics to avoid (sensitivity/controversial issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lists are determined by commander priorities and public needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media managers will engage with their audience at every opportunity but must exercise caution because responses reflect the commander and organization, not the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All responses, interactions, and endorsements are official reflections and must be handled accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited/inappropriate content on social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media sites must not contain inappropriate links, references revealing sensitive movements or locations of assets/personnel, classified or FOUO material, personal information protected by the Privacy Act, copyrighted material without permission, political endorsements, graphic/obscene/hateful/defamatory comments, or legal details about ongoing investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content must be cleared for public release; follow AR and relevant statutes (e.g., 17 USC for copyright, Privacy Act, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel security and OPSEC compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not post information revealing sensitive movements or locations where uncertainty is an element of security; review content for OPSEC before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content must be cleared for public release and avoid scientific/technical info not cleared, classified material, or FOUO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and trademark compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyrighted material may only be used with written permission; Government works are not copyright protected; trademarks and other marks must not be used without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AR 27–60 and U.S. copyright law (17 USC). Be cautious with software/code and other original works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political activity restrictions for official accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Army social media platforms will not engage in political conversations or show endorsements (shares, likes, reactions) to political statements, posts, graphics, or content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official accounts must remain nonpartisan and avoid any appearance of political endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leader account requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Command sergeants major and commanders from ACOMs, ASCCs, and DRUs must be registered to the social media directory and their platforms must follow official account requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders' personal/professional presence must comply with official-account policies when registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Readiness Group (FRG) page rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit FRG pages must adhere to DoD and Army requirements even if not in the directory; FRG pages must not exclude any member of the FRG’s parent unit and content must be approved by the unit's release authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRG pages can be open or closed groups but must comply with approval processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting page status and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages created and managed by U.S. Army recruiters and their commands are considered official pages and must abide by the same standards of conduct; unit commanders are responsible for enforcement and refining the digital footprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruiting pages are official; treat accordingly with release authority and registration where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and identity representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency is portraying oneself online truthfully without falsifying identity or credentials; do not forge or manipulate identifiers to impersonate or misrepresent affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid any manipulation of identifiers in posts that would disguise identity or affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on anonymous posts
rubrics_metrics.description: If platform technology allows users to post anonymously, organizations will allow such posts to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must handle anonymous posts per their policies and in compliance with other regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on private/closed third-party presences
rubrics_metrics.description: Official government use of private or closed social media groups on third-party platforms is not authorized; nonpublic information may not be released outside DoD networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If official closed groups are needed, host them behind a firewall on a DoD-approved network (e.g., milSuite, Intelink).

rubrics_metrics.name: External linking policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking to external sources via social media is permitted and encouraged provided links meet security, accuracy, propriety, and policy guidelines and follow platform user terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links should be related to the Army mission or its people; PA professionals must be educated consumers of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing commercial news content
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media managers may share individual commercial news articles if they support commander objectives, do not endorse the news organization, and represent factual information (not opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid appearance of preferential treatment when deciding whom to follow; if following one local news org, follow all local news networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of service and Federal-compatible agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to General Services Administration for negotiated federal-compatible terms of service agreements for social media and other digital tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GSA resources to ensure platform user terms are compatible with Federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting impostor accounts and scams
rubrics_metrics.description: Units are responsible for reporting impostors of their leaders and personnel to appropriate social media platforms and should follow OCPA Digital Media Division guidance for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report impostors and scams per provided Army guidance link and platform reporting mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and password management
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to official social media accounts must be carefully managed in unit SOPs; security settings maximized and include two-step verification if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat social media access and passwords with as much care as PII; include access management in continuity and SOPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-streaming control and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: All live streamed events should be constantly manned with a contingency plan to take them offline in the event of violence, crime, or imagery unsuited for public consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate on-duty personnel for live events and have immediate takedown procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and content boosting prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Units and social media managers are not authorized to use funds to advertise or boost content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not spend unit funds on paid promotions or boosting posts on platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and records management
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic messages and content created or received in the course of Army official business on social media platforms are federal records and must be scheduled for disposition; Army imagery used in social media platforms is considered a permanent, released DoD record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop processes and procedures for regular archiving of content; archive all VI (vital information) per regulation paragraph 3–4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonaccredited social media account compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media accounts are nonaccredited if the organization is not brigade level or above, is not open to the general public, or does not meet registration guidance; nonaccredited accounts still must be compliant with chapter guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonaccredited accounts must follow the same substantive rules even if not registered in the directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of social media in crisis communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media platforms must be integrated into Public Affairs planning as part of crisis communication efforts because they are the fastest way to inform the public regarding emerging or breaking news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow chapter 7 policies for crisis communication and release of official information; casualty release per DoDI 1300.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal use limitations and appropriate online conduct for Soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Soldiers may use personal social media but have limitations: may share publicly released unclassified DoD/DA info; must exercise judgment; consult supervisor or PA office if unsure; are prohibited from posting defamatory, obscene, abusive, illegal, copyrighted (without permission), trademark-infringing, privacy-infringing, nonpublic, or otherwise inappropriate information; cannot forge identifiers; fundraising use of service affiliation is restricted; should not use Government email to create personal accounts or invite participation via Government email; employees should not use official position on personal accounts unless accompanied by biographical facts including official photos; political activity must comply with JAG guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Soldiers remain subject to UCMJ; OPSEC and Hatch Act limits apply; ultimately individuals are responsible for their posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Army website (Army.mil) and CORE CMS usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Army.mil is the official webpage; CORE is the content management platform provided to Army PA personnel. Units may have CORE organization pages and PA officers are encouraged to register for CORE to publish content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content submitted to CORE must be reviewed and approved by authorized personnel for release per local chain of command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational website public-information policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All information on publicly accessible websites is public information and subject to the regulation's clearance and release procedures; official Army websites must comply with listed ARs and DoD instructions and must not contain nonreleasable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to AR 25–1, AR 25–22, AR 25–30, AR 380–5, AR 381–12, AR 530–1, and other cited policies for domain-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonreleasable website content categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Official public websites must not contain nonreleasable information such as classified information; casualty info before next-of-kin verification; Privacy Act-protected personal data; info on incidents under investigation; imagery of coalition forces without release or of enemy casualties; misrepresentative statements harmful to good order/morale; sensitive photographs (IED results, casualties); and HIPAA-protected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See DA Pam 25–1–1 for additional guidance on nonreleasable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website training for PA officials
rubrics_metrics.description: PA officials who post unclassified information to official websites and social media must complete the website training course offered through ALMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training applies to Soldiers, DA Civilians, and supporting contractors who review, post, and maintain Army content on non-Army.mil websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication editorial standards (factual and objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: News coverage and editorial content in DoD publications must be factual and objective; avoid morbid, sensational, or alarming details not essential to factual reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accuracy and balance; editorial policies should support commander responsibilities and the overall information program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free flow of news and prohibition on calculated withholding
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a free flow of news and information to all DA personnel without censorship or news management; calculated withholding of unfavorable news to DA is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial policy must not be used to suppress unfavorable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fact, opinion, editorials, and commentaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Army publications will distinguish between fact and opinion; editorials (command position) and commentaries (personal opinion) must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an opinion is expressed, the person or source will be identified to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and source-crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute opinions and information sources; news content should be based on releases, reports, and materials from DoD components and other government agencies and credit sources of material other than local internal sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution is essential to credibility; follow guidance on crediting sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance to avoid appearance of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid appearance of bias, commercial news and opinion articles should be balanced with opposing views, appearing in the same issue/page when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overseas command newspapers may include U.S. political campaign news on a balanced, impartial, nonpartisan basis per limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on political campaign content in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Army publications will not contain campaign news (except as specified in DoDI 5120.04), partisan discussions, cartoons, editorials, or commentaries dealing with political campaigns, candidates, or issues, or which advocate lobbying elected officials on specific issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications can present factual voting information per Federal Voting Assistance Program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polls, surveys, and straw votes compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Army publications conducting polls, surveys, or straw votes must comply with DoDI 1100.13, DoDI 8910.01, and DoDM 8910.01 Volumes 1 and 2; DoD components may authorize polls on local-interest matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use policy guidance for permissible topics (e.g., Soldier of the week) and compliance with survey rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication naming, ownership, and trademark coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where CE printer owns the name, steps should be taken to ensure Army owns and controls publication names; commanders must consult U.S. Army Legal Services Agency about proposed new publication names and possible trademark registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include legal consultation early to manage naming and trademark issues per AR 27–60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masthead content and disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: The masthead of all DoD publications must contain a disclaimer that the publication is authorized for DoD members and contents are not necessarily official views of the U.S. Government/DoD; funded publications must contain additional language as stipulated in DoDI 5120.04; CE publications have specific masthead language and contact listing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow type-size and wording requirements (e.g., CE masthead text printed no smaller than 6 points) and include required statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of color in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Color must be functional and add value to the publication; color will not be used merely for its own sake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should be sensitive to funding and justify color use by its contribution to communication effectiveness; AR 25–30 governs color processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian Enterprise (CE) publication controls
rubrics_metrics.description: CE publications (newspapers, magazines, guides, maps, websites) support internal communication and are authorized under DoDI 5120.04; only one CE guide and one CE installation map authorized per command; CE contracting and operations are subject to special rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CE contractor manages employment/administration of CE staff; military or DA civilian personnel will not be assigned duty on contractor premises for contractor business activities; conflicts of interest must be avoided and reported to servicing SJA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting provisions for CE guides and maps
rubrics_metrics.description: CE contracts for guides and installation maps must establish firm delivery dates and contain provisions ensuring distribution is controlled by the command; over-run copies and delivery dates may be specified for advertiser appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DoDI 5120.04 for CE guides/maps contract provisions and require geospatial office review for OPSEC risks on maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on implied DoD endorsement and advertising rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Army publications will not contain material that implies DoD component endorsement/favor of commercial products/services; will not subscribe to services whose primary purpose is advertising; will not carry advertisements that violate DoD equal opportunity policy. All commercial advertising must be clearly identified and paid advertorials labeled as advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid advertorials and supplements must be distinguishable from editorial content; refer to DoDI 5120.04 for handling ads that violate policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriated Funded (AF) publication policies
rubrics_metrics.description: AF newspapers/magazines/websites support command communications, are normally printed under contract, may be distributed through official channels, and expenses charged to the publishing command's appropriated funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended minimum circulation is one copy to three readers; both AF and CE publications must comply with AR 25–22 and mailing/distribution policies (AR 25–51). AF publications will not carry commercial advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial contributions and permission for outside material
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial contributions from stringers or local organizations may be used if permission is obtained and content does not violate regulation; editors may use bylines (rank optional but must be consistent); reviews may be included if no implication of Army selective benefit or endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting gratuities is prohibited; PA staff may accept press credentials; private organizations may have meeting announcements published without preferential treatment; CE/AF editors may edit letters and are not obligated to return unsolicited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on covering ongoing test/evaluation programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering ongoing test or evaluation programs is prohibited unless exceptions are approved through channels to OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for exceptions follow the channels described in the regulation (see para 6–6).
